doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

chapter: Denver youth and University of Denver
title: Learning form and hearing jazz artists in Denver clubs
summary: He realised tunes have forms; his father took him to hear Oscar Peterson, DeFranco and Gillespie.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Do you recall when you started figuring out the mystery of chord symbols and how they might apply to your improvising?

Yeah I do. When we got together to play it was just sort of a free for all you know. And I finally figured out oh, yeah, they’re playing the form and there’s a thing called a bridge you know. And you just don’t stop playing until you wear out and stop. You actually follow this form. So yeah, that dawned on me and I started listening to music more intently and talking to my friends. And also at that time my dad would take me to hear guys that would come into town, like Oscar Peterson and Buddy DeFranco and Dizzy Gillespie, and so he would take me to these you know they were bars, nightclubs, and I’d get to hear these guys and that was good. My dad wasn’t a musician or anything but he liked that music and so actually my mom would go too and sometimes my clarinet teacher would go — a clarinet teacher previous to the college one.
